calls.head: Who blinks first?
calls.body: The Oilers are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Devils are near the top at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Oilers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.
calls.call: The Oilers’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.7 expected goals per 60 against the Devils.

calls.head: The Devils like Mantha’s line against Formenton’s
calls.body: At home, the Devils keep sending Mantha’s line (Mantha, Rodrigues and Boqvist) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Sheldon Keefe keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Oilers’ third line is Formenton, Dickinson and Joseph.

NJD.head: We gave New Jersey a 60% chance, and they delivered.

EDM.head: We had Edmonton as slight underdogs (40%), and it went New Jersey’s way.

surprises.head: Edmonton couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Edmonton usually gets worse looks than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: a 2.6% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.2% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far less than once in a thousand games. You may never see it again.

story.head: Gritsyuk wins it in a shootout
paras: Evan Bouchard opened the scoring for the Oilers midway through the first. The second period was a wild one. Connor Brown tied it 1-1 for New Jersey on the power play early in the period. Jack Hughes scored midway through the period and again 45 seconds later to put the Devils up 3-1. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins pulled the Oilers within one on the power play less than three minutes later, and Leon Draisaitl tied it up on the power play early in the third. The shootout went four rounds, and Arseny Gritsyuk won it for the Devils after Jesper Bratt had scored earlier. Jack Hughes added an assist for a three-point night.

The Devils owned the chances, outshooting the Oilers 34-21, and still had to sweat it out in a shootout. Connor Hellebuyck made 18 saves for the Devils, and Tristan Jarry stopped 31 of 34 at the other end.

The Devils killed off a two-man advantage that lasted just over a minute late in the second. The Devils moved to 10-5-0, second in the Metropolitan, while the Oilers fell to 11-2-3 but climbed into first in the NHL in points percentage.

items.text: Jack Hughes passed Jesper Bratt for eighth on the Devils’ all-time goals list, with 176.
Connor McDavid has a point in all 16 games this season.
The Oilers’ three-game winning streak is over.
The Devils have beaten the Oilers five straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
